comparison/example-1.text: The updated booking system runs much faster than the old platform.

comparison/example-2.text: The Busan warehouse operates far more efficiently than the Incheon site.

comparison/story-1.text: Daniel is choosing a supplier for 200 new office chairs.

comparison/story-2.text: Hartwell's chairs cost slightly more than the chairs from Brightseat.

comparison/story-3.text: However, Hartwell delivers much faster than Brightseat, so the chairs would arrive before the office move.

comparison/story-4.text: Daniel decided that quick delivery matters more than a small price difference.

conjunction/example-1.text: Although the hotel was fully booked, the travel agent found two rooms for us.

conjunction/example-2.text: Although the deadline was tight, the design team finished the brochure on schedule.

conjunction/story-1.text: Although the train to Taichung was delayed, Kevin arrived before the client meeting started.

conjunction/story-2.text: Because the projector did not work, he presented the slides on his laptop.

conjunction/story-3.text: The client agreed to sign the contract provided that deliveries begin in March.

conjunction/story-4.text: Once the legal team reviews the terms, Kevin will send the final copy.

gerund-infinitive/example-1.text: The manager suggested moving the weekly meeting to Thursday afternoon.

gerund-infinitive/example-2.text: The board decided to open a second branch office in Singapore.

gerund-infinitive/story-1.text: The sales team planned to visit three clients in Seoul next month.

gerund-infinitive/story-2.text: Their director suggested booking the flights early to save money.

gerund-infinitive/story-3.text: However, the team postponed reserving hotel rooms until the schedule was confirmed.

gerund-infinitive/story-4.text: The travel agent encouraged them to buy travel insurance before leaving.

passive-voice/example-1.text: The new service contract was signed by both parties on Monday.

passive-voice/example-2.text: The damaged printer was returned by the customer last week.

passive-voice/story-1.text: Every order at Norland Supplies is packed within 24 hours.

passive-voice/story-2.text: Last Thursday, a large order from a hotel chain was shipped by express courier.

passive-voice/story-3.text: The next morning, the boxes were delivered to the wrong address.

passive-voice/story-4.text: The mistake was fixed by the logistics team, and the hotel received its order that afternoon.

preposition/example-1.text: The accounting office will process the invoice within five days.

preposition/example-2.text: The vendor must deliver the samples by next Monday.

preposition/story-1.text: A client in Taichung ordered 200 office chairs on Monday.

preposition/story-2.text: The supplier promised delivery within ten business days.

preposition/story-3.text: The purchasing team must approve the payment by Thursday.

preposition/story-4.text: Mr. Lin has been responsible for this account since last year.

pronoun/example-1.text: The new interns completed their safety training on the first day.

pronoun/example-2.text: The company updated its travel policy after the merger.

pronoun/story-1.text: The purchasing team reviewed its supplier list last week.

pronoun/story-2.text: Mr. Tanaka sent his recommendations to the finance director.

pronoun/story-3.text: Five suppliers had raised their prices, so several of them were removed from the list.

pronoun/story-4.text: The remaining suppliers will send their revised quotes by Friday.

quantifier/example-1.text: Neither of the proposals meets the budget limit for this year.

quantifier/example-2.text: One of the printers on the third floor needs a new toner cartridge.

quantifier/story-1.text: Ms. Lee received quotes from three hotels for the sales conference in May.

quantifier/story-2.text: Neither of the first two hotels has a room large enough for 200 guests.

quantifier/story-3.text: Each of the quotes includes breakfast, but only a few offer free parking.

quantifier/story-4.text: One of the event planners is visiting the third hotel tomorrow.

relative-clause/example-1.text: The consultant who reviewed our contracts will present the findings on Friday.

relative-clause/example-2.text: The assistant who arranged the flights will send the itinerary tomorrow.

relative-clause/story-1.text: A customer whose package arrived damaged called the support center on Monday.

relative-clause/story-2.text: The agent who took the call offered a full refund right away.

relative-clause/story-3.text: She also shipped a replacement from the warehouse where the company keeps its spare stock.

relative-clause/story-4.text: The next day, the customer posted a review that praised the quick response.

subjunctive/example-1.text: The director recommends that each department submit its budget by June.

subjunctive/example-2.text: The client insisted that the supplier replace the damaged parts.

subjunctive/story-1.text: The HR manager reviewed the company's hiring process last week.

subjunctive/story-2.text: She recommended that every candidate complete a short writing test.

subjunctive/story-3.text: The CEO also insisted that the team not schedule interviews on Fridays.

subjunctive/story-4.text: If the company had used this process last year, it would have avoided several costly hiring mistakes.

verb-tense/example-1.text: By the time the auditors arrived, the accounting team had already closed the books for the quarter.

verb-tense/example-2.text: By the time the shipment reached the port, the customer had canceled half of the order.

verb-tense/story-1.text: Mina flew to Osaka for a trade show last Monday.

verb-tense/story-2.text: By the time her flight landed, the exhibition hall had already opened.

verb-tense/story-3.text: Her colleague had set up the booth the night before.

verb-tense/story-4.text: By the time Mina reached the booth, three clients had left their business cards.

vocabulary/example-1.text: The director gave constructive comments on the hiring plan.

vocabulary/example-2.text: The marketing team conducted a customer survey on the new packaging.

vocabulary/story-1.text: Our office conducted a short survey on the new room booking system.

vocabulary/story-2.text: Most employees gave constructive feedback about its design.

vocabulary/story-3.text: However, access to the system is still restricted to managers.

vocabulary/story-4.text: The IT department agreed to extend the trial period until June.

word-form/example-1.text: The overseas supplier replied promptly to our price inquiry.

word-form/example-2.text: The temporary receptionist greeted the visitors politely during the conference.

word-form/story-1.text: Ms. Chen's department received an urgent complaint on Tuesday morning.

word-form/story-2.text: The new assistant answered the customer immediately.

word-form/story-3.text: Her careful explanation of the refund policy was very helpful.

word-form/story-4.text: The next day, the satisfied customer thanked the whole team warmly.
